text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government is owed 15 million Malta pounds ($39 million) in social security contributions, with Malta Drydocks topping the list of companies which have not passed workers' contributions on to the government.

- Government announces plans to tackle Malta's increasing traffic congestion. Roads will continue to be improved, the police traffic section will be enlarged and there will be greater emphasis on education of drivers.
- Italy to give Malta two rescue launches.

- Malta's ruling Labour Party insists on balance in public broadcasting. The party is locked in dispute with the Broadcasting Authority which last week ruled in favour of the opposition Nationalist Party about government advertisements on a new taxation system that has replaced VAT. The Nationalist Party had argued that the adverts included political controversy.
- Company salesman fends off hold-up by three men.
- Bulgarian family found living in Malta illegally.
- New tourism promotion emphasis on Turkey. The number of Turkish tourists visiting Malta is negligible, but an increasing number of Maltese are going there, lured by cheap holidays.
